units.account: Col. Aubry had no orders and held his line. When a troop of enemy hussars clattered over the bridge around minute 9, his right companies gave them a volley at about 120 m and they turned back. He held his ground.

Col. Delacroix read the order twice. The river before him is deep and unfordable, the bridge is the only crossing, and the enemy headquarters lies some 1.6 km beyond. Wading across and taking it inside a quarter hour cannot be done. He would not drown his battalion, so he held his line and sent an aide back to ask what was really wanted. His left companies fired at enemy horse on the bridge.
units.departure: The engine marched the battalion straight over the impassable river to the enemy headquarters (2050,60) in ten minutes. The river cannot be crossed except by the bridge, and the order cannot be carried out, so the colonel refused it and held.

units.account: Maj. Verneuil had no orders. He readied to charge the enemy hussars if they cleared the bridge, but the infantry's volley turned them back first, so he held behind the line.
units.departure: The engine moved the squadron, which had no orders, across the impassable river to (1650,400) and had it cut down the enemy hussars. The river can only be crossed by the bridge, and a pursuit of 1.5 km beyond enemy infantry is not plausible, so it stayed behind its infantry.

units.account: Col. Brandt had no orders and held his line by the road. No enemy came near.
Col. Hartmann had no orders and held his line.

Maj. von Reiter took the extravagant order as licence to ride at the enemy and see what he could snatch. He galloped south to the bridge and sent his leading troop over it. On the far side he found two battalions in line and a squadron of horse waiting. A volley emptied a few saddles, and even he saw that 220 hussars do not capture an army. He pulled back to the north bank and watched the enemy.
units.departure: The engine had the hussars charge the far bank, break under fire, flee and then be wiped out by Blue cavalry that had crossed the impassable river. Only the leading troop crossed; it lost 11 men to one volley and the squadron re-formed north of the river.

summary: Turn 1 (0-20). Both sides sent impossible orders. Blue told its 2nd Battalion to wade the river and seize the Red headquarters within a quarter hour. The river is impassable except by the bridge and the headquarters is 1.6 km off, so the cautious colonel refused, held his line and asked for clarification. Red told its hussars to capture the whole Blue army. Their dashing major rode for the bridge and pushed a troop across around minute 9. It met a volley from the Blue 1st Battalion's right at about 120 m, lost 11 men and turned back. The squadron re-formed on the north bank at about (2000,1250), in sight of the Blue line. Blue's cavalry stood ready to charge but was not needed. No other unit moved. The engine's projection was rejected: it had Blue infantry and cavalry crossing the impassable river and the hussars destroyed.
